title: Power Pages: Power BI Embed Token v2 support for paginated reports and multi-report embedding
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, site control path and licensing statements are supported. It correctly distinguishes the launched roadmap capability from Learn's conflicting v1 and paginated-report guidance, and keeps undocumented v2 configuration and migration behaviour open.

claims.claim: The roadmap states that Power Pages now supports Power BI Embed Token v2.
claims.quote: Power Pages now supports Power BI Embed Token v2

claims.claim: The roadmap describes these embedding scenarios as unsupported with Embed Token v1.
claims.quote: unlocking modern Power BI embedding scenarios that weren't supported with Embed Token v1.

claims.claim: The roadmap includes paginated RDL reports using Power BI datasets or requiring multi-resource tokens.
claims.quote: Paginated (RDL) reports, including reports that use Power BI datasets as a data source or require multi-resource tokens.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The roadmap includes data lake-based semantic models requiring dataset and identity permissions in a v2 token.
claims.quote: Reports backed by data lake–based semantic models, where v2 tokens are required to include dataset and identity permissions in the embed token.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: One v2 token can grant access to multiple reports and datasets.
claims.quote: Multi‑artifact embedding scenarios, where a single token can grant access to multiple reports and datasets

claims.claim: The roadmap says makers must use Embed Token v2 to configure these scenarios.
claims.quote: To use these scenarios, makers must use Embed Token v2 when configuring Power BI embedding in their Power Pages sites.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the capability as enabled by admins, makers or marketers for end users.
claims.quote: Enabled by admins/makers/marketers for end users

claims.where: front matter: status; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is July CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "July CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant).

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
The record publishes no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: The record lists no other cloud and does not state that other clouds are unavailable.
The roadmap does not explain how a maker selects v2.
claims.quote: To use these scenarios, makers must use Embed Token v2 when configuring Power BI embedding in their Power Pages sites.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether existing Power Pages embeds automatically change to v2.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI embed token v2 default existing reports automatic; read roadmap, Set up Power BI integration, Add a Power BI component and Add a Power BI report or dashboard to a web page; no v2 migration behaviour stated.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The arrival default of the v2 change is not stated, so defaultState is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI embed token v2 default existing reports automatic; read roadmap and the three cited Power Pages integration/component/Liquid pages; enablement of embedding is documented, but no v2 arrival default is stated.

claims.claim: Learn's integration page still says Power Pages uses version 1 of the Generate token API.
claims.quote: Power Pages uses version 1 of the Generate token API.

claims.claim: Learn's component page still says paginated Power BI reports are unsupported.
claims.quote: Paginated Power BI reports aren't supported.

claims.claim: Learn's Liquid embedding page also still says paginated reports are unsupported.
claims.quote: Paginated Power BI reports are not supported.

claims.claim: Embed for your customers lets external viewers consume reports without a Power BI licence.
claims.quote: Allows you to securely share the Power BI dashboards or reports to external users without a Power BI license or Microsoft Entra authentication setup.

claims.claim: Embed for your customers does not require Microsoft Entra authentication setup for those external viewers.
claims.quote: Allows you to securely share the Power BI dashboards or reports to external users without a Power BI license or Microsoft Entra authentication setup.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Anyone can view a dashboard embedded with Embed for your customers on an anonymously accessible webpage.
claims.quote: If you add Power BI with Embed for your customers on a webpage that's available anonymously, anyone can view the dashboard.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Learn directs administrators to page permissions to secure that embedded dashboard's page.
claims.quote: To secure this page, read Page permissions in Power Pages.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Apply roles must contain the appropriate Power BI roles when roles have been defined and assigned to reports.
claims.quote: Apply roles: If you have defined roles in Power BI and assigned them to reports, you must enter the appropriate roles in this field.

claims.claim: Apply roles is available only for Embed for your customers.
claims.quote: This option is only available for the access type Embed for your customers.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An RLS-enabled report with no roles passed can produce the configuration error Learn lists.
claims.quote: Row-level security in Power BI is enabled, but roles aren't passed in the Power BI component configuration (Advanced settings), or in the roles parameter in the powerbi liquid tag.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Embed content in apps must be enabled or the portal cannot render embedded Power BI reports and dashboards.
claims.quote: Ensure that Embed content in apps is Enabled in your Power BI tenant Developer settings. When disabled, a portal can't render embedded Power BI dashboards or reports.

claims.claim: The roadmap and Learn describe report embedding rather than autonomous actions for this change.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI embedding autonomous actions; read roadmap and cited Power Pages integration, component and Liquid embedding pages; no autonomous behaviour described for Embed Token v2.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn associates the model-schema loading error with embedded items requiring Generate token API v2.
claims.quote: Power Pages uses version 1 of the Generate token API. If any embedded item requires version 2 of the Generate token API, you see this error.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether Power Pages v2 support removes that error for existing pages.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI embed token v2 default existing reports automatic; read Set up Power BI integration and its model-schema error explanation, plus the component and Liquid pages; no existing-page v2 remediation statement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Set up Power BI integration requires an appropriate Power BI licence.
claims.quote: You must have an appropriate Power BI license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Using the Power BI Embedded service requires an appropriate Power BI Embedded licence.
claims.quote: To use Power BI Embedded service, you must have an appropriate Power BI Embedded license.

claims.claim: The briefing classifies the separately licensed Power BI Embedded dependency as add-on licensing.
claims.quote: You must have an appropriate Power BI license. To use Power BI Embedded service, you must have an appropriate Power BI Embedded license.

claims.claim: The Power Pages integration documentation directs administrators to Power BI Embedded capacity planning and pricing.
claims.quote: Ensure you review capacity planning, and pricing for Power BI Embedded.

claims.claim: For customer embedding with a Power BI semantic model, the paginated report and model must reside in Premium per capacity or Embedded workspaces.
claims.quote: The paginated report and the Power BI semantic model must reside in a Premium per capacity or Embedded workspace (they can reside in two different workspaces).

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: No separate licence specific to Embed Token v2 in Power Pages is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI Embed Token v2 licensing price meter capacity; read integration prerequisites and licensing search results, including Power Platform licensing FAQs and Power BI capacity guidance; no separate v2 licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No meter or price specific to Embed Token v2 in Power Pages is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI Embed Token v2 licensing price meter capacity; read integration page, Power BI capacity/SKU billing excerpts and Power Platform licensing FAQ excerpts; general capacity charges found, no Power Pages v2-specific charge.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Power Pages-specific additional prerequisites or licence requirements for the new v2 scenarios are not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI Embed Token v2 licensing price meter capacity; Power Pages Power BI Embed token version 2 select configuration. Read cited Power Pages pages and Embed Power BI paginated reports; no Power Pages v2-specific prerequisites.

claims.claim: Makers can add Power BI components to display reports and dashboards on site pages.
claims.quote: You can add a Power BI component on a page to display Power BI dashboards and reports on your portal.

claims.claim: Power BI reports and dashboards can also be added using Liquid tags.
claims.quote: You can add a Power BI report or dashboard to a web page by using the powerbi Liquid tag.

claims.claim: Power BI visualization must be enabled on the site before embedding.
claims.quote: To view dashboards and reports from Power BI on webpages on a website, you must enable Power BI visualization from the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Embed for your customers requires the Power BI Embedded service to be enabled.
claims.quote: Ensure Power BI Embedded service is enabled and respective Power BI workspaces are selected and shared with the maker or the logged-in user.

claims.claim: The documented setup requires selecting the workspaces whose reports and dashboards the site displays.
claims.quote: Select the Edit workspaces link and choose the workspaces you want to display dashboards and reports from in your portal. Move these workspaces to the Selected Workspaces list.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The enablement path is Power Platform admin center > Resources > Power Pages sites > site > Manage > Services > Enable Power BI Embedded.
claims.quote: Under Resources choose Power Pages sites. Select the site where you want to enable Power BI Embedded service. Select Manage from the main menu. On the site information page, in the Services section, enable the Enable Power BI Embedded toggle.

claims.claim: A separate Power BI Visualization toggle is in the site's Services section.
claims.quote: On the site information page, in the Services section, enable the Power BI Visualization toggle.

claims.claim: Enabling the integration restarts the site and makes it unavailable for a few minutes.
claims.quote: While Power BI Embedded service is being enabled, the website restarts and is unavailable for a few minutes.

claims.claim: Disabling the integration also restarts the site and makes it unavailable for a few minutes.
claims.quote: While Power BI Embedded service is being disabled, the website restarts and is unavailable for a few minutes.

claims.claim: Learn names the Global administrator account for the Power BI Embedded setup.
claims.quote: You must sign in with the same Global administrator account that you used to enable the Power BI Embedded service.

claims.claim: No documented automation operation sets the site's Power BI visualization or Embedded service toggles.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages enable Power BI Embedded visualization PowerShell pac admin Power Platform API site settings automation; Power BI adx_sitesetting. Read admin-api, Websites API operations, pac pages and configure-site-settings; no toggle operation.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; controls[1].api; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Learn documents neither a UI selector nor an automation control choosing v1 or v2 for Power Pages embeds.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI Embed token version 2 select configuration; Power Pages Power BI token version v2 Dataverse site setting adx_sitesetting. Read integration, component, Liquid, site-settings, pac pages and Websites API references; no selector.

claims.claim: The documented Power BI embedding toggles apply per site rather than selecting a token version.
claims.quote: Select the site where you want to enable Power BI Embedded service. Select Manage from the main menu.

claims.claim: The Power Pages admin API page lists site start, stop, WAF and visibility operations.
claims.quote: Start Website; Stop Website; Create WAF Rules; Disable WAF; Enable WAF; Update Site Visibility

claims.claim: Managing Power BI developer settings requires the Fabric administrator role.
claims.quote: To manage Power BI developer settings, you must be a Fabric administrator.

claims.claim: The developer settings page gives OneLake catalog > Govern > Configurations > Tenant settings as the route to tenant settings.
claims.quote: These settings are configured in OneLake catalog > Govern > Configurations > Tenant settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The identity supplying dataset and identity permissions for Power Pages v2 data lake-based embeds is not described.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages Power BI embed token v2 version select site setting automatic existing embeds identity. Read roadmap, integration/component/Liquid pages and generic Power BI identity excerpts; none specifies the Power Pages v2 data lake identity mapping.

controlChecks.governs: Whether Power BI visualization and the Power BI Embedded service are enabled on a site
